concept.text: A proof or disproof that on a non-singular complex projective algebraic variety every Hodge class is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic cycles. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Resolution of the rational Hodge conjecture
page.definition: A proof or disproof that every rational cohomology class of type (p,p) on every smooth complex projective variety, a nonsingular space defined by homogeneous polynomial equations, is a rational combination of classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties. Type (p,p) means representability by closed differential forms with p holomorphic and p antiholomorphic factors.

goal.need: On a smooth complex projective fourfold, geometers can recognize the classes of divisors and curves by their Hodge type. For surfaces they can do this only in special cases. A proof would let them infer, for example, that an isomorphism of rational cohomology preserving the Hodge decomposition of two such varieties comes from an algebraic cycle on their product. A counterexample would identify a rational class for which the Hodge type gives the wrong answer. Even a positive answer allows rational combinations of subvarieties with negative coefficients.

statements.quote: with $1 million allocated to the solution of each problem.
statements.context: The seven Millennium Prize Problems include the Hodge conjecture.

statements.quote: the establishment of seven Millennium Prize Problems: the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, the Hodge conjecture
statements.context: Clay announced the problems in Paris on 24 May 2000. Its president recalled the announcement in the institute’s 2010 annual report.

completion.title: Clay accepts a complete resolution of the rational Hodge conjecture after its own examination.
completion.criterion: CMI accepts a complete solution after examination under §7(a)(ii). The solution either proves that every rational Hodge class on every smooth projective complex variety is a rational combination of algebraic cycle classes, or gives a counterexample CMI judges to resolve the problem under §5(c)(i). At least two years must have elapsed since qualifying publication, and the solution must have survived at least two years of rigorous community examination and gained general acceptance. A smaller award under §5(c)(ii) leaves the problem open in reformulated form.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §§4–7.
completion.threshold_quote: at least two (2) years have elapsed since publication of the Proposed Solution in a Qualifying Outlet
completion.basis: Clay specifies the rational conjecture and separates community acceptance from its subsequent examination. The latter provides an externally adjudicated endpoint.

milestones.title: Every rational Hodge class of degree 2 on a smooth projective complex variety is algebraic.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth projective complex variety X, every class in H²(X,ℚ) ∩ H¹˒¹(X) is a rational linear combination of the classes of irreducible codimension-one subvarieties of X.
milestones.set_by: The field's Lefschetz (1,1) theorem; recorded in Deligne's official Clay problem description, §2(iii).
milestones.threshold_quote: shows that c is the first Chern class of a line bundle.

milestones.title: The rational Hodge conjecture holds for every smooth projective complex variety of dimension at most 3.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth projective complex variety X of complex dimension at most 3 and every codimension p, the rational cohomology classes of type (p,p) are spanned over ℚ by classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties of X.
milestones.set_by: The field's established low-dimensional theorem, reported in Clay Mathematics Institute's official Hodge overview.
milestones.threshold_quote: when the solution set has dimension less than four.

milestones.title: Every rational Hodge class of degree 4 on every smooth complex cubic fourfold is algebraic.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth cubic hypersurface X in complex projective 5-space, each rational cohomology class of degree 4 and type (2,2) is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic surfaces in X.
milestones.set_by: The field's rational Hodge conjecture restricted to cubic fourfolds; Zucker, Theorem 3.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: We derive the Hodge Conjecture for cubic fourfolds

milestones.title: A proposed solution gains general acceptance after at least two years of community examination.
milestones.criterion: A complete proof or proposed resolving counterexample appears in a Qualifying Outlet under §6. At least two years have elapsed since that publication. The solution has survived rigorous examination by the global mathematics community for at least two years and gained general acceptance, as determined by CMI.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §§4, 6 and 7(a)(i).
milestones.threshold_quote: The Proposed Solution must survive rigorous examination by the global mathematics community for a minimum of two (2) years.

milestones.title: Algebraic curves span the rational Hodge classes of degree 2n − 2 on every smooth projective complex n-fold.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n ≥ 1, each rational cohomology class of degree 2n − 2 and type (n − 1,n − 1) is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic curves in X.
milestones.set_by: The curve-class corollary of the Lefschetz theorems, stated by Voisin in Some aspects of the Hodge conjecture, §2.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Hodge conjecture (for projective varieties) is always true for rational Hodge classes of degree 2n − 2.

milestones.title: The rational Hodge conjecture holds for every complex abelian variety of dimension at most five.
milestones.criterion: For every complex abelian variety A of dimension at most 5 and every codimension p, each rational cohomology class of type (p,p) on A is a rational linear combination of classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties of A.
milestones.set_by: The rational Hodge conjecture for low-dimensional abelian varieties, as stated in Markman’s Corollary 1.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Hodge conjecture holds for abelian varieties of dimension ≤ 5.

results.finding: On every smooth complex projective variety, rational Hodge classes of degree 2 are spanned by divisor classes.
results.detail: Deligne presents the proof in §2(iii) and attributes it to Kodaira and Spencer’s 1953 journal paper.
results.quote: shows that c is the ﬁrst Chern class of a line bundle.

results.finding: The rational Hodge conjecture holds for all smooth projective complex varieties of dimension at most 3.
results.detail: The Clay Mathematics Institute states the established result on its official problem page.
results.quote: The Hodge conjecture is known in certain special cases, e.g., when the solution set has dimension less than four.

results.finding: Curve classes generate degree-4 Hodge classes on all uniruled threefolds and all regular threefolds with trivial canonical bundle.
results.detail: The source presents the author’s proof sketch for these families. It identifies the original publication as a contribution to an edited volume and gives no peer-review or proof-assistant record for this result.
results.quote:
Theorem 17 Let X be a uniruled threefold, or a regular threefold with trivial canon-
ical bundle. Then the Hodge conjecture is satisﬁed by integral Hodge classes of degree
4 on X, that is, integral Hodge classes of degree 4 are generated by classes of curves
in X.

results.finding: On every smooth complex cubic fourfold, algebraic surface classes span all rational Hodge classes of degree 4.
results.detail: The rational finding is established by Zucker’s journal paper cited in the text. The supplied document identifies itself as expanded Takagi lecture notes and gives no journal publication information for its own version.
results.quote:
Theorem 18 Let X be a cubic fourfold. Then any integral Hodge class on X is
algebraic.

results.finding: On every smooth complex projective n-fold with n ≥ 1, algebraic curves span the rational Hodge classes in degree 2n − 2.
results.detail: The supplied manuscript gives the Lefschetz argument for n ≥ 2. The dimension-one case follows directly from the classes of the connected components. The text supplies no publication or peer-review information for this manuscript.
results.quote:
The Hodge conjecture
is then true for rational Hodge classes of degree 2 n−2, that is, degree 2 n−2 rational
cohomology classes of Hodge type ( n − 1, n − 1) are algebraic, which means that
they are the cohomology classes of algebraic cycles with Q-coeﬃcients.

results.finding: On every smooth complex cubic fourfold, rational surface classes generate all degree-4 rational Hodge classes.
results.detail: Remark 5.9 derives the rational-surface generation statement from the earlier integral proof cited as [32]. The statement is universal, so there is no finite sample size.
results.quote:
the group of Hodge classes
of degree 4 on a cubic fourfold is generated by classes of rational surfaces.
